Implement `verifyVoucher(token, secret, currentSecond)` using only Node.js standard-library APIs. A voucher is `<body>.<signature>`, where `body` is the base64url encoding of UTF-8 JSON and `signature` is the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of the body text using `secret`. `secret` must be a nonempty string and `currentSecond` a nonnegative safe integer. Verification must occur inside the returned Promise so every failure becomes a rejection. Reject malformed tokens, invalid signatures, JSON arrays, and payloads that lack a nonempty string `subject` or nonnegative safe-integer `expiresAt`. Use a constant-time comparison for equal-length signatures. A voucher is expired when `expiresAt` is less than or equal to `currentSecond`; reject it with an `Error` whose `code` is `VOUCHER_EXPIRED`. Resolve valid vouchers with the newly parsed payload object. Do not mutate or retain caller-owned mutable data. Export exactly the function with `module.exports = verifyVoucher`.
